def-qsm-identical-particle-fock-sectors:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $I$ be a specified finite or countably infinite
mode set with a fixed enumeration, and let $\mathfrak h=\ell^2(I)$ have its
coordinate orthonormal basis $(e_j)_{j\in I}$. Put
$\mathfrak h^{\otimes 0}=\mathbb C$, $\mathfrak h^{\otimes 1}=\mathfrak h$,
and define each completed tensor power recursively by
$\mathfrak h^{\otimes(n+1)}=\mathfrak h^{\otimes n}\widehat\otimes\mathfrak h$,
using the first-variable-linear product inner product of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. For $n\ge1$, let
$U_\pi$ permute the tensor factors for $\pi\in S_n$, and let
$$
P_\pm^{(n)}=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\chi_\pm(\pi)U_\pi, \qquad \chi_+(\pi)=1,\quad \chi_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),
$$
with $P_\pm^{(0)}=I_{\mathbb C}$. The permutation-sector theorem
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] makes these orthogonal
projections. Define the symmetric and antisymmetric sectors
$\mathcal H_\pm^{(n)}:=\operatorname{ran}P_\pm^{(n)}$. Define
$$
\mathcal F_\pm(\mathfrak h):=\left\{\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\ge0}:\psi_n\in\mathcal H_\pm^{(n)},\ \sum_{n\ge0}\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\right\}, \qquad \langle\psi,\varphi\rangle:=\sum_{n\ge0}\langle\psi_n,\varphi_n\rangle.
$$
The vector $\Omega=(1,0,0,\ldots)$ is the vacuum, and the finite-particle
subspace consists of vectors with only finitely many nonzero components.

This is a mathematical construction for a specified mode basis. Choosing its
symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a physical species is a separate model
postulate. No spin-statistics theorem or physical species assignment is part of
the definition.
lem-qsm-fock-occupation-basis-and-car-re:
## Statement

Let $I$ and $\mathcal F_\pm(\ell^2(I))$ be as in
[[def-qsm-identical-particle-fock-sectors]]. Define
$$
\Omega_B:=\{m:I\to\mathbb N_0:m\text{ has finite support}\},\qquad \Omega_F:=\{m:I\to\{0,1\}:m\text{ has finite support}\}.
$$
For either statistics choice, write $|m|=\sum_jm_j$. If $m\in\Omega_B$, choose the elementary tensor $x_m$ containing $m_j$ copies of each mode $j$ in the fixed order and set
$$
|m\rangle_B:=\sqrt{\frac{|m|!}{\prod_jm_j!}}\,P_+^{(|m|)}x_m.
$$
If $m\in\Omega_F$, list its occupied modes increasingly in the fixed enumeration, let $x_m$ be their elementary tensor and set
$$
|m\rangle_F:=\sqrt{|m|!}\,P_-^{(|m|)}x_m.
$$
For $|m|=0$, both vectors are the vacuum. These vectors form orthonormal bases and define unitary identifications $\mathcal F_+(\ell^2(I))\cong\ell^2(\Omega_B)$ and $\mathcal F_-(\ell^2(I))\cong\ell^2(\Omega_F)$.

On the finite-support span $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ of the bosonic basis, define
$$
a_j|m\rangle_B=\sqrt{m_j}|m-\mathbf1_j\rangle_B,\qquad a_j^\dagger|m\rangle_B=\sqrt{m_j+1}|m+\mathbf1_j\rangle_B,
$$
where the annihilation term is zero when $m_j=0$. Their maximal closed extensions have domains
$$
D(a_j)=\left\{c:\sum_{m\in\Omega_B}m_j|c_m|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad D(a_j^\dagger)=\left\{c:\sum_{m\in\Omega_B}(m_j+1)|c_m|^2<\infty\right\},
$$
and $a_j^\dagger=a_j^*$. On $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$, they satisfy
$[a_i,a_j^\dagger]=\delta_{ij}I$, $[a_i,a_j]=0$, and $[a_i^\dagger,a_j^\dagger]=0$.

On the fermionic basis define
$$
c_j|m\rangle_F=(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}m_i}m_j|m-\mathbf1_j\rangle_F,\qquad c_j^\dagger|m\rangle_F=(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}m_i}(1-m_j)|m+\mathbf1_j\rangle_F.
$$
These operators are bounded on the full fermionic Fock space and satisfy
$\{c_i,c_j^\dagger\}=\delta_{ij}I$ and $\{c_i,c_j\}=\{c_i^\dagger,c_j^\dagger\}=0$. These are mathematical sector relations; they do not select a physical species or imply a spin-statistics theorem.
lem-qsm-models-diagonal-occupation-trace:
## Statement

Assume [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $I$ be finite or countably infinite with a specified enumeration, let $m\in\Omega_\pm$ be the occupation configurations of [[lem-qsm-fock-occupation-basis-and-car-relations]], and let $\epsilon_j\in\mathbb R$ be finite mode energies. For each finite-support configuration put
$$
E(m):=\sum_j\epsilon_jm_j,\qquad N(m):=|m|=\sum_jm_j.
$$
These are finite sums. On $\ell^2(\Omega_\pm)$, define the real diagonal multipliers
$$
D(H)=\left\{c:\sum_mE(m)^2|c_m|^2<\infty\right\},\quad (Hc)_m=E(m)c_m,
$$
$$
D(N)=\left\{c:\sum_m|m|^2|c_m|^2<\infty\right\},\quad (Nc)_m=|m|c_m,
$$
and, for $\mu\in\mathbb R$,
$$
D(K_\mu)=\left\{c:\sum_m|E(m)-\mu|m||^2|c_m|^2<\infty\right\},\quad (K_\mu c)_m=(E(m)-\mu|m|)c_m.
$$
Each is self-adjoint on its displayed domain. No equality between $D(K_\mu)$ and $D(H)\cap D(N)$ is asserted.

For $\beta>0$, set $q_j=e^{-\beta(\epsilon_j-\mu)}$. In the bosonic case assume
$$
0<q_j<1,\qquad q_*:=\sup_jq_j<1,\qquad \sum_jq_j<\infty;
$$
Here $q_*=0$ by convention when $I$ is empty; for nonempty $I$ the displayed supremum is unchanged. In the fermionic case assume $q_j>0$, $\sum_jq_j<\infty$, and only finitely many gaps $\epsilon_j-\mu$ are negative. Define the positive diagonal multiplier $G_{\beta,\mu}$ by $G_{\beta,\mu}|m\rangle=e^{-\beta(E(m)-\mu|m|)}|m\rangle$. Then $G_{\beta,\mu}$ is trace class, with
$$
\Xi_B=\operatorname{Tr}G_{\beta,\mu}=\prod_j(1-q_j)^{-1}<\infty,\qquad \Xi_F=\operatorname{Tr}G_{\beta,\mu}=\prod_j(1+q_j)<\infty.
$$
Thus $\rho_{\beta,\mu}=\Xi^{-1}G_{\beta,\mu}$ is a positive trace-class operator of trace one. Its finite-mode marginals are independent: bosonic occupation $n_j\in\mathbb N_0$ has law $(1-q_j)q_j^{n_j}$, and fermionic occupation $n_j\in\{0,1\}$ has probabilities $(1+q_j)^{-1}$ and $q_j(1+q_j)^{-1}$. In particular
$$
\mathbb E_BN_j=\frac{q_j}{1-q_j},\quad \operatorname{Var}_B(N_j)=\frac{q_j}{(1-q_j)^2},\qquad \mathbb E_FN_j=\frac{q_j}{1+q_j},\quad \operatorname{Var}_F(N_j)=\frac{q_j}{(1+q_j)^2}.
$$
The total number has finite mean and variance under the stated mode conditions. The trace hypotheses alone do not imply finite energy moments or differentiability in $\beta,\mu$.

For an additional compact-parameter envelope, the corresponding response identities hold. For fixed $\mu$, if for every compact $B\subset J\subset(0,\infty)$ a summable $(a_m)$ satisfies $(1+|E(m)-\mu|m||^2)e^{-\beta(E(m)-\mu|m|)}\le a_m$ for all $m$ and $\beta\in B$, then $-\partial_\beta\log\Xi=\mathbb E(K_\mu)$ and $\partial_\beta^2\log\Xi=\operatorname{Var}(K_\mu)$. If $(\beta,\mu)$ varies over an open set and a summable compact-parameter envelope dominates $e^{-\beta(E(m)-\mu|m|)}(1+|E(m)|^2+|m|^2)$, then at fixed $\beta$, $\partial_\mu\mathbb E(N)=\beta\operatorname{Var}(N)$ and $\partial_\mu\mathbb E(E)=\beta\operatorname{Cov}(E,N)$. These stronger moment envelopes are additional hypotheses, not consequences of trace-class normalization.

For a finite mode set $J$, the canonical fixed-number coefficients are defined by
$$
\prod_{j\in J}(1-ze^{-\beta\epsilon_j})^{-1}=\sum_{N\ge0}Z_{B,N}(J)z^N,\qquad \prod_{j\in J}(1+ze^{-\beta\epsilon_j})=\sum_{N=0}^{|J|}Z_{F,N}(J)z^N.
$$
Each coefficient is the sum of the Boltzmann weights over the corresponding number sector; for a countable mode set it is the increasing limit over finite mode sets and is finite under the stated grand-trace hypotheses. A fixed-number law is the grand law conditioned on total number, so its occupations are generally coupled. The oscillator specialization uses the actual one-particle Hermite basis and diagonal domain of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]], not a formal differential eigenfunction list.
thm-qsm-models-lattice-riemann-bose-boun:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, $\alpha,\beta>0$, and $h>0$. Define
$F_B(p)=(e^{\beta\alpha|p|^2}-1)^{-1}$ for $p\ne0$ and
$F_F(p)=(e^{\beta(\alpha|p|^2-\mu)}+1)^{-1}$ for finite $\mu\in\mathbb R$.
For each $\mu<0$, both $F_B(\cdot;\mu)=(e^{\beta(\alpha|p|^2-\mu)}-1)^{-1}$ and $F_F$ are continuous, and for every fixed integer $s\ge0$ their polynomially weighted lattice sums converge with
$$h^d\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}|hk|^sF(hk)\longrightarrow\int_{\mathbb R^d}|p|^sF(p)\,dp\quad(h\downarrow0).$$
The convergence is uniform when $(\beta,\mu)$ ranges over a compact subset of $\{\beta>0,\mu<0\}$ for bosons or $\{\beta>0,\mu\in\mathbb R\}$ for fermions. At the singular Bose endpoint $\mu=0$, if $d>2$, then
$$h^d\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}}F_B(hk)\longrightarrow\int_{\mathbb R^d}F_B(p)\,dp=(\pi/(\beta\alpha))^{d/2}\sum_{\ell=1}^\infty\ell^{-d/2}.$$
The last series is finite exactly for $d>2$. No value is assigned to $F_B(0)$.

post-qsm-models-statistics-and-preparati.physical_scope: Adoption of nonrelativistic Hilbert-space state and Born-probability language, a specified Hamiltonian and interaction, a chosen symmetric boson or antisymmetric fermion sector, and a canonical or grand-canonical Gibbs preparation only when its trace is positive and finite. This formulation asserts no spin-statistics theorem, thermalization dynamics, universal equilibrium, empirical observation, or applicability to a particular species.

post-qsm-models-statistics-and-preparati:
## Postulate

For a declared nonrelativistic quantum model, adopt a complex Hilbert space, positive trace-one states, and Born probabilities for its specified measurements. Specify the one-particle modes, Hamiltonian and interactions. When the modeled particles are assigned bosonic or fermionic statistics, choose the symmetric or antisymmetric sector, respectively, as an independent physical assumption. This selection is not derived from the Fock construction or a nonrelativistic spin-statistics theorem.

For a canonical preparation at inverse temperature $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$, adopt $\rho=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta H}$ on the declared fixed-particle-number sector only when $0<Z=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H}<\infty$. For a grand-canonical preparation with chemical potential $\mu$, adopt $\rho=\Xi^{-1}e^{-\beta(H-\mu N)}$ only when the corresponding trace is finite and positive, as explicitly checked for the diagonal Fock model in [[lem-qsm-models-diagonal-occupation-trace]]. Fixed-number and grand-canonical preparations are distinct assumptions; in general the latter has independent mode occupations while conditioning on fixed total number couples them.

The assignments of $U=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho H)$, $S=-k_B\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)$ and thermodynamic potentials are model definitions where their traces exist. An identification with measured macroscopic thermodynamic quantities requires a separate physical bridge. No thermalization mechanism, empirical value, or law for a particular material is postulated here.

pthm-qsm-dilute-occupation-limit.physical_scope: Conditional mode-by-mode approximation for a trace-class ideal Bose or Fermi grand state with dimensionless fugacities 0<q_j≤r<1 and summable squared fugacities. The occupation and log-partition errors are bounded explicitly. This is a controlled dilute or low-fugacity limit, not a high-temperature criterion, universality statement, interacting-gas result, or empirical observation.

pthm-qsm-dilute-occupation-limit:
## Statement

Assume the preparation postulate [[post-qsm-models-statistics-and-preparation]] and the diagonal grand-trace hypotheses of [[lem-qsm-models-diagonal-occupation-trace]]. Let the mode set be finite or countable, with $0<q_j\le r<1$ and $\sum_jq_j^2<\infty$. Write $\bar n_j^B=q_j/(1-q_j)$ and $\bar n_j^F=q_j/(1+q_j)$. Then
$$|\bar n_j^B-q_j|\le\frac{q_j^2}{1-r},\qquad |\bar n_j^F-q_j|\le q_j^2,$$
and the total occupation approximation error is bounded by the corresponding summable right-hand sides. The grand log partition factors obey
$$0\le -\log(1-q_j)-q_j\le\frac{q_j^2}{2(1-r)},\qquad 0\le q_j-\log(1+q_j)\le\frac{q_j^2}{2}.$$
Thus the classical Maxwell–Boltzmann first-order terms have a controlled aggregate error under the stated squared-summability hypothesis.

pthm-qsm-oscillator-spin-ensembles.physical_scope: Exact canonical calculations for the one-dimensional harmonic oscillator with its proved Hermite spectral realization and for a declared independent two-level spin Hamiltonian. The low- and high-temperature limits retain the model's zero-point and ground-degeneracy qualifications. No generic third-law claim, species magnetic moment, material prediction, or measurement is asserted.

pthm-qsm-oscillator-spin-ensembles:
## Statement

Assume [[post-qsm-models-statistics-and-preparation]]. Let $\omega>0$, $m>0$, $\hbar>0$, $k_B>0$, and $T>0$; set $\epsilon=\hbar\omega$ in joules and $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$. Take the self-adjoint one-dimensional realization $H_{\rm osc}$ of $-\hbar^2(2m)^{-1}d^2/dx^2+m\omega^2x^2/2$ on $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$ with Hermite eigenvectors $\phi_n$, eigenvalues $\epsilon(n+1/2)$, and domain $D(H_{\rm osc})=\{\sum_nc_n\phi_n:\sum_n\epsilon^2(n+1/2)^2|c_n|^2<\infty\}$, as proved in [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]].
$$Z=e^{-\beta\epsilon/2}(1-e^{-\beta\epsilon})^{-1},\quad U=\epsilon(\tfrac12+\bar n),\quad \bar n=(e^{\beta\epsilon}-1)^{-1},\quad C_V=k_B(\beta\epsilon)^2\frac{e^{\beta\epsilon}}{(e^{\beta\epsilon}-1)^2}.$$
Its entropy is $S=k_B[(1+\bar n)\log(1+\bar n)-\bar n\log\bar n]$; as $T\downarrow0$, $U\to\epsilon/2$, $S,C_V\to0$. As $\beta\epsilon\downarrow0$, $U=\beta^{-1}+O(\beta\epsilon^2)$.

For a separate two-level spin model $H_s=-h\sigma_z$ with $h\in\mathbb R$ in joules, $Z_s=2\cosh(\beta h)$, $U_s=-h\tanh(\beta h)$, $C_{V,s}=k_B(\beta h)^2\operatorname{sech}^2(\beta h)$, and $S_s\to0$ as $T\downarrow0$ when $h\ne0$, whereas $S_s=k_B\log2$ when $h=0$. These results make no generic third-law claim.

pthm-qsm-periodic-ideal-occupation.physical_scope: A finite-volume ideal gas defined spectrally on the integer momentum labels of a periodic box, with dispersion alpha|2pi k/L|^2 and a finite internal degeneracy g. It proves finite grand trace, exact mode means and continuum density/energy limits for fixed mu<0 in the Bose case or finite mu in the Fermi case. It does not identify this spectral definition with a differential operator domain, claim a finite-volume phase transition, or establish an empirical gas model.

pthm-qsm-periodic-ideal-occupation:
## Statement

Adopt the model preparation of [[post-qsm-models-statistics-and-preparation]]. Let $d\ge1$, $L,m,\hbar,k_B,T>0$, $V=L^d$, $\alpha=\hbar^2/(2m)$, $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$, and let $g\in\mathbb N$ count distinct internal modes. Define the one-particle Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^d\times\{1,\ldots,g\})$ with diagonal energies $\epsilon_k=\alpha|2\pi k/L|^2$ and domain $\sum_{k,s}\epsilon_k^2|c_{k,s}|^2<\infty$. This is a spectral periodic-box model; no differential-operator realization is required.

For bosons take $\mu<0$; for fermions take any finite $\mu\in\mathbb R$. In either case the grand trace is finite, mode occupations are independent in the adopted grand state, and
$$\bar n_{k,s}=\frac1{e^{\beta(\epsilon_k-\mu)}\mp1},\qquad \operatorname{Var}(N_{k,s})=\bar n_{k,s}(1\pm\bar n_{k,s}),$$
with the upper sign choice in the denominator interpreted as $-$ for bosons and $+$ for fermions (equivalently the variance is $\bar n(1+\bar n)$ for bosons and $\bar n(1-\bar n)$ for fermions). For fixed $\beta,\mu$ in these regimes, as $L\to\infty$,
$$\frac{\mathbb E N}{V}\to\frac{g}{(2\pi)^d}\int_{\mathbb R^d}\frac{dp}{e^{\beta(\alpha|p|^2-\mu)}\mp1},\qquad \frac{\mathbb E H}{V}\to\frac{g}{(2\pi)^d}\int_{\mathbb R^d}\frac{\alpha|p|^2\,dp}{e^{\beta(\alpha|p|^2-\mu)}\mp1}.$$
The continuum limits are conditional model deductions; they assert no thermalization or measured density.

pthm-qsm-fermi-zero-temperature.physical_scope: The continuum grand-state density and energy and its fixed-density zero-temperature endpoint for a three-dimensional homogeneous ideal Fermi dispersion alpha|k|^2 with finite internal degeneracy g. The zero-temperature results are conditional ideal-gas predictions, with no Sommerfeld expansion, material-specific model, or reported observation.

pthm-qsm-fermi-zero-temperature:
## Statement

Under the ideal spectral gas model of [[pthm-qsm-periodic-ideal-occupation]], specialize to $d=3$ and $\alpha=\hbar^2/(2m)>0$. For finite $\mu$ and $\beta>0$, the continuum number and energy densities are
$$\rho(\mu,\beta)=\frac{g}{(2\pi)^3}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{d^3k}{e^{\beta(\alpha|k|^2-\mu)}+1},\quad u(\mu,\beta)=\frac{g}{(2\pi)^3}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\alpha|k|^2d^3k}{e^{\beta(\alpha|k|^2-\mu)}+1}.$$
For each $\rho>0$ and $\beta>0$ there is a unique $\mu(\rho,\beta)$ giving that density. As $\beta\to\infty$, $\mu(\rho,\beta)\to E_F$ and $u\to(3/5)\rho E_F$, where
$$k_F=(6\pi^2\rho/g)^{1/3},\qquad E_F=\alpha k_F^2.$$
The ideal grand thermodynamic pressure $p$ defined by
$$p=\frac{g}{\beta(2\pi)^3}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\log(1+e^{-\beta(\alpha|k|^2-\mu)})d^3k$$
satisfies $p=2u/3$; hence its zero-temperature endpoint is $2\rho E_F/5$.

pthm-qsm-homogeneous-bose-condensation.physical_scope: A sequence of three-dimensional or dimension-d ideal, homogeneous, quadratic-dispersion grand states on periodic boxes whose chemical potentials are chosen to hold the mean particle density fixed. It proves the critical density, dimension restriction, and grand-ensemble zero-mode nonconcentration. It does not assert canonical-ensemble equivalence, trapping, interactions, superfluidity, a finite-volume phase transition, or empirical condensation.

pthm-qsm-homogeneous-bose-condensation:
## Statement

Adopt the homogeneous periodic Bose model of [[pthm-qsm-periodic-ideal-occupation]] with one internal mode ($g=1$), dimension $d\ge1$, $\alpha=\hbar^2/(2m)>0$, fixed $\beta>0$ and target mean number density $\rho>0$. For each $L$, choose the unique $\mu_L<0$ solving
$$L^{-d}\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}(e^{\beta(\alpha|2\pi k/L|^2-\mu_L)}-1)^{-1}=\rho.$$
Define $\rho_c=(2\pi)^{-d}\int_{\mathbb R^d}(e^{\beta\alpha|p|^2}-1)^{-1}dp$ as an extended nonnegative number. Then $\rho_c=(4\pi\beta\alpha)^{-d/2}\sum_{\ell\ge1}\ell^{-d/2}$; it is finite exactly when $d>2$. For $d\le2$, $\mathbb E N_0/L^d\to0$ for every finite $\rho$. For $d>2$, $\mathbb E N_0/L^d\to(\rho-\rho_c)_+$, where $(x)_+=\max(x,0)$. When $d=3$, $\rho_c=\lambda_T^{-3}\zeta(3/2)$, $\lambda_T=(2\pi\hbar^2\beta/m)^{1/2}$, and the positive mean condensed fraction below $T_c=[2\pi\hbar^2/(mk_B)](\rho/\zeta(3/2))^{2/3}$ is $1-(T/T_c)^{3/2}$.

If $d>2$ and $\rho_0=\rho-\rho_c>0$, the grand-state ground occupation satisfies
$$\operatorname{Var}(N_0/L^d)\to\rho_0^2,\qquad \mathbb P(N_0/L^d\ge x)\to e^{-x/\rho_0}\quad(x>0).$$
In particular the condensate density does not converge in probability to its mean limit in this grand ensemble.

ex-qsm-dilute-occupation-limit.physical_scope: A one-mode exact comparison of Bose, Fermi, and first-order classical occupations at q=1/2, with no empirical interpretation.

ex-qsm-oscillator-spin-ensembles.physical_scope: A direct low-temperature comparison of the one-dimensional harmonic oscillator and the zero-field two-state spin model covered by the linked theorem. It records a model result, not a universal third-law statement or observation.

ex-qsm-periodic-ideal-occupation.physical_scope: An exact two-mode, one-particle canonical calculation compared with the distinct grand-canonical independent-mode preparation; no ensemble-equivalence claim is made.

ex-qsm-fermi-zero-temperature.physical_scope: A three-dimensional ideal Fermi sea at fixed density, calculating its Fermi wave number, mean energy per particle, and grand thermodynamic pressure from the linked zero-temperature theorem. It is not a material equation of state or measured pressure.

ex-qsm-homogeneous-bose-condensation.physical_scope: The grand-ensemble ground-mode variance and tail at a fixed positive excess density above the ideal critical density, as a direct instance of the linked theorem. It makes no canonical or interacting-gas claim.
